title: Microsoft Azure Quiz
description: Revisit the key ideas in Microsoft Azure. Read each choice carefully. You can try the quiz again after reviewing the lessons.

questions.question: What should come before choosing services?
options: A large shopping list of resources
questions.explanation: Microsoft Azure offers rented services for computing, storage and networking. A useful design begins with the job, not with the longest list of services. The page files can be delivered without creating an account system for visitors.

questions.question: What groups related Azure resources?
questions.explanation: An Azure subscription is a billing and management boundary. A resource group collects related resources for a project. The group gives related resources a shared management container. Resource-level settings still matter.

questions.question: Should regional feature support be checked?
questions.explanation: An Azure region is a geographic area. Many regions offer availability zones, which provide separate physical locations within the region. Service features vary by region. A region name alone does not guarantee every feature is available.

questions.question: What does identity describe?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID manages identities. An identity can represent a person, application or workload, depending on how access is arranged. Identity answers who is asking. A permission assignment answers what that identity may do.

questions.question: What does scope decide?
questions.explanation: Azure role-based access control assigns a role to an identity at a scope. Scope can be a resource, resource group or broader boundary. The reviewer can inspect resources at that scope without getting general edit permission from this assignment.

questions.question: What is stored inside a container?
questions.explanation: Azure Blob Storage keeps objects called blobs. Containers group blobs inside a storage account. The account, container and blob are three different levels. The blob name can contain slashes.

questions.question: What does static hosting execute on the server?
options: Every browser JavaScript file as a server program
questions.explanation: An Azure Storage static website uses an index document and an error document. It is a way to serve files, not an application backend. The index opens the site; the error document helps when a page is missing. A real site also needs correct routing and domain configuration.

questions.question: Who must plan VM software upkeep?
questions.explanation: An Azure virtual machine is a configurable computer in the cloud. Its operating system and software still need care. A VM may be useful for a separate experiment, but it is unnecessary for many static pages.

questions.question: What does a subnet divide?
questions.explanation: A virtual network provides a private network space. Subnets divide that space into smaller address ranges for resources. The example subnet ranges are separate. Network routes and access rules decide how traffic moves.

questions.question: Which rule priority is considered earlier?
questions.explanation: A network security group contains rules that allow or deny network traffic. Rules have priorities, so their order matters. A smaller priority number is processed before a larger one. The full rule set determines the result.

questions.question: Does an alert explain every cause automatically?
questions.explanation: Azure Monitor collects supported metrics and logs. Alerts can tell you when a chosen condition is met. The alert calls attention to a symptom. Someone still needs to find and fix its cause.

questions.question: What must cleanup target?
questions.explanation: Azure budgets can notify you about spending. Review actual resource costs and plan cleanup; notifications are not a general guarantee that spending stops. These numbers teach a budget calculation, not a real service price.
